hero.title: Long-running Claude：面向科学计算的长任务 Agent 工作流
hero.en: The article explains how to run multi-day Claude Code workflows for scientific computing using memory, test oracles, and orchestration.
hero.zh: 文章说明如何用记忆文件、测试判据和编排循环，把 Claude Code 用于跨天运行的科学计算任务。

summary.lead: 这篇文章的重点不是让 Agent 盲目自治，而是为长时间科学计算任务建立可恢复、可验证、可监督的运行框架。

cards.title: 任务要有判据
cards.body: 适合 Agent 的科学任务通常范围清晰、成功标准明确，并且可以对照 reference implementation 或测试套件验证。

cards.title: 记忆必须外置
cards.body: CHANGELOG.md 把进展、失败路线、精度表和限制沉淀为可携带长期记忆，避免重复走死路。

cards.title: 运行要可恢复
cards.body: Git、tmux、SLURM 和提交规则把无人值守运行变成可观察、可恢复的工程流程。

cards.title: 编排补足能力
cards.body: Ralph loop 等模式在模型能力不足时提供脚手架，防止过早声称完成。

keyPoints.label: 核心判断
keyPoints.text: 长任务 Agent 的可靠性来自明确目标、测试判据、持久记忆和可恢复执行环境。

keyPoints.label: 边界条件
keyPoints.text: 这种方法适合成功标准清楚的工程化科学任务，不等同于开放式科学发现自动化。

keyPoints.label: 实践收益
keyPoints.text: 在合适问题上，Agent-driven development 可以把研究者数月到数年的实现工作压缩到数天级别。

sections.title: 哪些科学计算任务适合长时间 Agent

rows.en: Reimplementing a numerical solver, converting old Fortran software, and debugging against a reference implementation are good fits.
rows.zh: 重写数值求解器、迁移旧 Fortran 软件、对照参考实现调试，都是适合场景。

rows.en: The key prerequisites are well-scoped work, clear success criteria, and occasional rather than continuous human oversight.
rows.zh: 关键前提是范围清晰、成功标准明确，且不需要持续人工监督。

sections.title: 从 C 编译器到宇宙学 Boltzmann solver

rows.en: Claude previously worked across roughly 2,000 sessions to build a C compiler capable of compiling the Linux kernel.
rows.zh: Claude 曾跨约 2,000 个 session 构建可编译 Linux kernel 的 C 编译器。

rows.en: The article's concrete example is a differentiable cosmological Boltzmann solver in JAX.
rows.zh: 本文案例是在 JAX 中实现可微分的宇宙学 Boltzmann solver。

sections.title: 为什么 differentiable solver 有意义

rows.en: CLASS and CAMB are core scientific infrastructure for constraining cosmological models.
rows.zh: CLASS 和 CAMB 是约束宇宙学模型的核心科学基础设施。

rows.en: A differentiable solver propagates gradients and enables gradient-based inference, speeding up parameter estimation.
rows.zh: 可微分 solver 能传播梯度，支持基于梯度的推断，并加速参数估计。

sections.title: 长任务 Agent 的三个支点

rows.en: CLAUDE.md carries instructions and context for the overall plan.
rows.zh: CLAUDE.md 承载总体计划和规则。

rows.en: CHANGELOG.md acts as portable long-term memory and lab notes.
rows.zh: CHANGELOG.md 是可携带长期记忆和实验记录。

rows.zh: test oracle 告诉 Agent 科学代码是否真的在进步。

sections.title: 用 Git、tmux 和 SLURM 管理无人值守运行

rows.en: Git makes progress visible, recoverable, and less likely to be lost when compute allocation ends.
rows.zh: Git 让进展可见、可恢复，也降低计算资源结束时丢失工作的风险。

rows.en: tmux lets Claude Code keep running on a compute node while the human detaches and checks occasionally.
rows.zh: tmux 让 Claude Code 在计算节点上持续运行，人类可断开后偶尔查看。

sections.title: 反复确认完成状态的编排模式

rows.en: The Ralph loop asks whether the agent is really done when it claims completion.
rows.zh: Ralph loop 在 Agent 声称完成时追问是否真的完成。

rows.en: The Ralph loop can be useful for long-running tasks since the agent will admit the task is not up to spec, and continue working until it is.
rows.zh: Ralph loop 对长任务有用，因为 Agent 会承认任务尚未达到规格，并继续工作直到达标。

rows.en: Claude reached sub-percent agreement across outputs, though the resulting solver was not production-grade.
rows.zh: Claude 在多个输出上达到亚百分比一致性，但结果并非生产级。

rows.en: The article argues that not running agents now carries an opportunity cost when projects have well-defined success criteria.
rows.zh: 文章认为，当项目有清晰成功标准时，不运行 Agent 本身也有机会成本。

rows.en: Science Mar 23, 2026
rows.zh: 中文提示：本段为原文完整内容，关键内容请对照左侧英文阅读。

rows.caption: 原文封面图：Long-running Claude for scientific computing。

rows.en: In this post, Siddharth Mishra-Sharma, a researcher on the Discovery team, explains how to apply multi-day agentic coding workflows—test oracles, persistent memory, and orchestration patterns—to scientific computing tasks even outside of one’s domain.
rows.zh: 本文介绍如何把多日 Agent 编码工作流、测试判据、持久记忆和编排模式用于科学计算任务，即使任务不属于操作者的核心专业领域。

rows.en: Most scientists currently using AI agents work in a conversational loop, managing each step of the process on a tight leash. As models have become significantly better at long-horizon tasks over the last year or so, a new way of working emerged: rather than getting involved with every detail, we can specify the high-level objective and set a team of agents loose to work autonomously. This makes it possible to complete projects in mere hours that might otherwise take us days, weeks, or even months. Certain types of scientific tasks fit well within this model, e.g., reimplementing a numerical solver, converting legacy scientific software written in an old Fortran dialect to a modern language, and debugging a large codebase against a reference implementation. These are tasks where the work is well-scoped, the success criteria are clear, and human oversight can be occasional rather than continuous.
rows.zh: 作者指出，许多科学家仍逐步控制 AI Agent；随着模型长程任务能力提升，可以只给高层目标，让 Agent 团队更自主地推进工作。

rows.en: Anthropic’s C compiler project demonstrated a version of this, where Claude worked across roughly 2,000 sessions to build a C compiler capable of compiling the Linux kernel. This post describes how to set up a similar pattern for scientific computing tasks using Claude Code, with a typical academic lab in mind. As a concrete example, I will walk through using Claude Opus 4.6 to implement a differentiable version of a cosmological Boltzmann solver. This is numerical code that predicts the statistical properties of the afterglow of the Big Bang—the Cosmic Microwave Background, or CMB. It does this by evolving coupled equations for photons, baryons, neutrinos, and dark matter through the early universe.
rows.zh: 中文提示：本段为原文完整内容，关键内容请对照左侧英文阅读。

rows.en: Boltzmann solvers like CLASS and CAMB are core pieces of scientific infrastructure in cosmology, allowing us to constrain cosmological models using data from surveys like Planckand theSimons Observatory. A differentiable version—one that can propagate gradients through the full solver—enables the use of gradient-based inference methods, dramatically speeding up parameter estimation. Writing it in JAX is a natural fit here, since it gives us automatic differentiation and compatibility with accelerators (e.g., GPUs) essentially for free.
rows.zh: 中文提示：本段为原文完整内容，关键内容请对照左侧英文阅读。

rows.en: Notably, the task isn’t in my core scientific domain—I have a high-level familiarity with the tools and the science, but don’t have the expertise to complete it myself in any reasonable time frame. Groups who do have that expertise have built differentiable solvers in JAX with a subset of the features present in CLASS. These efforts typically represent months to years of researcher-time. The point here was to see if an agent could go further with minimal steering from a non-domain expert.
rows.zh: 该任务并非作者核心领域，实验目标是验证非领域专家能否通过少量引导让 Agent 推进高难科学计算项目。

rows.en: This kind of task is structurally different from the C compiler project, which can be farmed out to a large number of parallel agents. A Boltzmann solver, on the other hand, is a deeply coupled pipeline—a small numerical error or poor approximation in modeling how the early universe recombines can subtly shift everything downstream. It thus requires a different set of agent skills. Debugging requires tracing causally through the entire chain and drawing from domain knowledge, which may be better suited to a single agent working sequentially, spawning subagents as needed, and using the reference implementation to bisect discrepancies.
rows.zh: Boltzmann solver 是强耦合流水线，微小数值误差会传导到下游，因此更适合单 Agent 顺序推进并按需派生子 Agent。

rows.en: We'll use an HPC cluster running the SLURM job scheduler as our compute environment, but the core ideas—a progress file, a test oracle, an agent prompt with clear rules—apply regardless of where you run Claude Code.
rows.zh: 作者使用运行 SLURM 的 HPC 集群，但核心方法是进度文件、测试判据和规则明确的 Agent prompt。

groups.group: Draft a plan and iterate locally · 起草计划并在本地迭代

rows.en: In this shift toward managing an autonomous research team of agents, you should spend most of your time (in consultation with Claude), crafting a set of instructions that clearly articulates the project’s deliverables and relevant context. These instructions should live in a CLAUDE.md file located in the root directory. Claude treats this file specially, keeping it in context and referencing it for the overall plan. Crucially, Claude can edit these instructions as it works, updating them for future work as it works through issues.
rows.zh: 在管理自主研究 Agent 团队时，人的主要工作是与 Claude 一起打磨项目交付物、上下文和规则，并写入 CLAUDE.md。

rows.en: Here is an early CLAUDE.md for the cosmological Boltzmann solver project, showing the overall plan and design decisions codified after an initial attempt at writing the solver. To arrive at this, I specified the high-level goals of the project—achieving full feature-parity with the reference CLASS implementation while being fully differentiable, and having an accuracy target of 0.1% against CLASS in the main science deliverables—and iterated with Claude until the plan seemed satisfactory. Given that 0.1% is the typical level of agreement between the two canonical Boltzmann codes CLASS and CAMB, this seemed like a good science target.
rows.zh: 作者用早期 CLAUDE.md 固化总体计划和设计决策，目标是与 CLASS 达到 0.1% 精度一致。

groups.group: Memory across sessions · 跨会话记忆

rows.en: The progress file, which by convention we call here CHANGELOG.md, is the agent’s portable long-term memory, acting as a sort of lab notes. In CLAUDE.md, Claude was instructed to keep track of progress in this file.
rows.zh: CHANGELOG.md 作为 Agent 的可携带长期记忆，类似实验室笔记，用来记录进展。

rows.en: A good progress file might track current status, completed tasks, failed approaches and why they didn't work, accuracy tables at key checkpoints, and known limitations. The failed approaches are important—without them, successive sessions will re-attempt the same dead ends. An entry might look like: “Tried using Tsit5 for the perturbation ODE, system is too stiff. Switched to Kvaerno5.” Here is the changelog for the running example, showing these elements.
rows.zh: 好的进度文件应记录状态、已完成任务、失败路线、精度表和已知限制，避免后续会话重复死路。

groups.group: The test oracle · 测试判据

rows.en: While more open-ended scientific discovery via agents is certainly on the horizon, long-running autonomous scientific work today crucially depends on the agent having a way to know whether it’s making progress. For scientific code, this could be a reference implementation, a clearly quantifiable objective, or an existing test suite. It can also be helpful to instruct the agent to expand the test suite and run tests as it works, to prevent regressions. In my example task, Claude was instructed to construct and continuously run unit tests using CLASS C source as a reference implementation.
rows.zh: 长时间自主科学工作需要清晰判据：参考实现、可量化目标或现有测试套件。

groups.group: Git as coordination · 用 Git 协调

rows.en: Git can be a good way to monitor and coordinate the agent’s progress in a hands-off manner. The agent should commit and push after every meaningful unit of work. This gives you a recoverable history if something goes awry, makes progress visible locally, and prevents work from being lost if, for instance, your compute allocation runs out mid-session.
rows.zh: Git 能让人低接触地监控和协调 Agent 进展，并在计算资源中断时保留可恢复历史。

rows.en: Practically, this could be a set of instructions in CLAUDE.md, e.g. “Commit and push after every meaningful unit of work. Run pytest tests/ -x -q before every commit. Never commit code that breaks existing passing tests.”
rows.zh: CLAUDE.md 可规定每个有意义工作单元后提交、提交前跑测试、不得提交破坏既有测试的代码。

rows.en: For steering the agent, you can always SSH into the cluster and manually re-prompt and/or update its instructions. It is typically more ergonomic to simply ask a local instance of Claude Code to SSH in and run commands for you; this will also apply to everything described below.
rows.zh: 需要引导时可以 SSH 到集群重新提示或更新指令，也可以让本地 Claude Code 代为执行。

groups.group: The execution loop · 执行循环

rows.en: As mentioned above, it’s often useful to first iterate on the plan locally until you have one that looks reasonable and is encoded in CLAUDE.md. From there, start a Claude Code session inside a terminal multiplexer like tmux on a compute node, tell the agent where to find your codebase, and let it cook. Because the session runs inside tmux, you can detach, close your laptop, and occasionally check on progress (in the case of the Boltzmann solver, I would check in on GitHub on my phone, e.g. while waiting in line for a coffee).
rows.zh: 执行循环通常先本地迭代计划，再在计算节点的 tmux 中启动 Claude Code，使任务可断开后继续运行。

rows.en: On an HPC cluster you might request a node through the SLURM scheduler, and an example job script that launches Claude Code in a tmux session might look like the following:
rows.zh: 在 HPC 集群上可通过 SLURM 申请节点，并用脚本启动 tmux 中的 Claude Code 会话。

rows.en:
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=claude-agent
#SBATCH --partition=GPU-shared
#SBATCH --gres=gpu:h100-32:1
#SBATCH --time=48:00:00
#SBATCH --output=agent_%j.log
cd $PROJECT/my-solver
source .venv/bin/activate
export TERM=xterm-256color
tmux new-session -d -s claude "claude; exec bash"
tmux wait-for claude
rows.zh: 代码示例：原文给出的可执行命令或配置片段。

rows.en: Once the job starts, you attach to the tmux session, give Claude Code direction (e.g., “Read CHANGELOG.md and pick up the next task”), and detach when you're satisfied it's on the right track. You can re-attach whenever you want to check in, steer, or start a new task using something like:
rows.zh: 任务启动后，连接 tmux、让 Claude Code 读取 CHANGELOG.md 并继续下一项任务，然后可断开并稍后重新接入。

rows.en: srun --jobid=JOBID --overlap --pty tmux attach -t claude
rows.zh: 代码示例：原文给出的可执行命令或配置片段。

rows.en: The Ralph loop: As models get more capable, they require less bespoke orchestration such as prompt engineering, RAG, or context stuffing. At a given point in time, however, it can be useful to provide some level of scaffolding as a capability uplift. For example, current models can suffer from agentic laziness—when asked to complete a complex, multi-part task, they can sometimes find an excuse to stop before finishing the entire task (“It’s getting late, let’s pick back up again tomorrow?”).
rows.zh: Ralph loop 会在 Agent 声称完成时把它拉回上下文，追问是否真的完成，用于缓解过早停止。

rows.en: To circumvent this, a useful orchestration pattern is the Ralph loop, which is essentially a for loop which kicks the agent back into context when it claims completion, and asks if it’s really done. This can be useful for long-running tasks since the agent will admit the task is not up to spec, and continue working until it is. Other similar patterns include GSD (and domain-specific variants) as well as the native-to-Claude Code /loop command.
rows.zh: Ralph loop 本质上是一种循环编排，帮助长任务 Agent 承认未达标并继续工作。

rows.en: Ralph can be installed via /plugin. A typical invocation prompt in Claude Code could look like
rows.zh: Ralph 可通过插件安装，并可设置最大迭代次数和完成承诺。

rows.en: /ralph-loop:ralph-loop “Please keep working on the task until the success criterion of 0.1% accuracy across the entire parameter range is achieved.” --max-iterations 20 --completion-promise “DONE”
rows.zh: 代码示例：原文给出的可执行命令或配置片段。

rows.en: Here, Claude will iterate up to 20 times until it guarantees that the task is done with a “DONE” incantation.
rows.zh: Claude 会最多迭代指定次数，直到以约定标记保证任务完成。

rows.en: Claude worked on the project from scratch over a few days, reaching sub-percent agreement with the reference CLASS implementation across its various outputs. I asked Claude to reconstruct the accuracy of some of the main outputs of the code—the various CMB angular power spectra—over the course of the project, also labeling milestones during development. It produced the plot below, illustrating the path to sub-percent accuracy.
rows.zh: Claude 从零推进项目数日，使多个输出与 CLASS 参考实现达到亚百分比一致，并生成精度路径图。

rows.caption: 原文图表：The path to sub-percent accuracy over time as the agent worked on the codebase.

rows.en: The path to sub-percent accuracy over time as the agent worked on the codebase.
rows.zh: 中文提示：本段为原文完整内容，关键内容请对照左侧英文阅读。

rows.en: The agent’s development trajectory was somewhat clunky. For example, there were clear gaps in its test coverage—for a while it was only testing the code at a single (fiducial) parameter point, drastically reducing its bug-catching surface area. It can also make elementary mistakes, such as tripping over gauge conventions or spending hours chasing bugs that a cosmologist would spot instantly, but it kept making sustained progress towards the stated goal of sub-percent accuracy.
rows.zh: 开发过程并不顺滑，测试覆盖曾有明显缺口，也会犯领域专家很快能发现的错误，但仍持续逼近目标。

rows.en: A side effect of the project was that I learned a surprising amount about Boltzmann solvers and the physics they model by watching the git commit history. The project isn’t drawn from my core scientific domain, but following Claude’s incremental progress and looking up what I didn't recognize turned out to be an effective way to osmose the science. The commit log reads like lab notes from a fast, hyper-literal postdoc.
rows.zh: 作者通过观察提交历史学到了不少 Boltzmann solver 物理知识，提交日志像快速而字面化的实验笔记。

rows.en: While the resulting solver is not production-grade (e.g., it doesn’t match the reference CLASS implementation to an acceptable accuracy in every regime), it demonstrates that agent-driven development can compress months or even years of researcher work into days.
rows.zh: 结果不是生产级，但证明 Agent 驱动开发能把数月或数年的研究工作压缩到几天。

rows.en: This kind of compression changes what counts as idle time. A universal experience in AI research is to launch an experiment (e.g., a training run) overnight and then have the satisfaction of seeing the results in the morning. Not running the experiment comes with an opportunity cost. These days, not running agents feels like it has a cost as well. If you have the compute and projects with well-defined success criteria, every night you don't have agents working for you is potential progress left on the table.
rows.zh: 这种压缩改变了 idle time 的含义：如果有算力和清晰成功标准，不运行 Agent 也意味着机会成本。
